Commentary.Commentary: ... THE RUN CHASE ...

The bowling from West Indies was superb but only till the 15th over as in the last 5 overs they went for aplenty. Akeal Hosein was the standout bowler, particularly in the Power Play, where he was virtually unplayable. He picked up two crucial wickets, setting the tone for the hosts. Obed McCoy also had a good outing, claiming two wickets and maintaining a tight leash on the Bangladesh batters. Romario Shepherd and Roston Chase chipped in with a wicket each as well.

We've reached the halfway mark in this T20I encounter, and Bangladesh has managed to post a competitive total of 147 runs after being put in to bat. The start was far from ideal for Bangladesh, as they lost wickets in quick succession, slumping to 30/3 inside the Power Play. However, Soumya Sarkar and Jaker Ali provided much-needed stability to the innings, stitching together a 57-run partnership that helped to revive the Bangladesh batting. Just when it seemed like the momentum was shifting in Bangladesh's favor, the wickets started to fall again. But then, Shamim Hossain and Mahedi Hasan took center stage, playing crucial cameos to propel the Bangladesh total past the 140-mark. Both Shamim and Mahedi scored in their 20s, injecting some much-needed impetus into the innings.
Good length on the pads, Rishad Hossain flicks this towards deep backward square and runs could to close the inning. Bangladesh post 147 on baord.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities and all set to go now. Soumya Sarkar and Tanzid Hasan Tamim will open the batting for Bangladesh. It will be Akeal Hosein to start with the ball for the home side. Let's play...

The teams and match officials make their way to the ground for the National Anthems. We start with the anthem of St Vincent and the Grenadines, followed by that of Bangladesh and the West Indies. Live action is not far away.

Litton Das, the Bangladesh skipper says that it looks like a good wicket to bat on. Adds that anything above 180 is a good total in his opinion. Mentions that he is used to leading the side and is happy with the opportunity. Shares that the conditions were different at this venue when they last played in the World Cup but he is happy to bowl second on this pitch. Ends by adding that they are going with 6 batters and 5 bowlers with two all-rounders in between them.

Rovman Powell the West Indies skipper wins the toss and opts to bowl first. He says that it looks like a very good surface. Adds that they want to see how Bangladesh bats on this wicket and then hopefully they chase it down. Mentions that it's a beautiful venue to play and a lot of fans have gathered. Shares that they are going with six batters, with Romario Shepherd as the all-rounder, Gudakesh Motie and Akeal Hossein as the two spinners, along with Andre Fletcher.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das(C)(WK), Shamim Hossain, Tanzid Hasan, Soumya Sarkar, Afif Hossain, Jaker Ali, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Mahedi Hasan, Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Johnson Charles, Nicholas Pooran(WK), Andre Fletcher, Rovman Powell(C), Romario Shepherd, Roston Chase, Akeal Hosein, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Obed McCoy.
Toss Update - West Indies have won the toss and opted to BOWL first in this contest.

On the flip side, Bangladesh are coming off a whitewash in the ODIs and will be keen to change their fortunes in the T20Is. Litton Das will lead the side in the absence of their regular skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto and the side will look to play a more attacking brand of cricket in the T20Is. Shamim Hossain, Ripon Mondol, and Mahedi Hasan are some of the fresh faces in the squad who will be itching to make a mark if given the chance. The visitors last played a T20I series against India and were clean swept in the three-match series. Bangladesh will look to be more competitive and challenge the Men in Maroon. So, which side are you backing to draw early blood in the series? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the three-match T20I series between the West Indies and Bangladesh from the Arnos Vale Ground in Kingston, St Vincent. After making a clean sweep of the one-dayers, the home will try to replicate a similar effort in the game's shortest format. Rovman Powell continues to lead the side in this format with Nicholas Pooran, Akeal Hosein, Johnson Charles, and Obed McCoy joining the side for the T20Is and will be looking to make a significant impact for the home side. The West Indies last played a T20I series against England in November and lost by a 1-3 margin. The home side will look to put that behind them and start on a positive note.
...MATCH DAY...

The Bangladesh tour of the West Indies has reached its final chapter, and the stage is set for an electrifying three-match T20I series. After a gritty 1-1 draw in the Tests and a dominant 3-0 ODI sweep by the Windies, both sides will be eager to leave their mark in the shortest format. The Arnos Vale Stadium in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is ready to host the opening clash, with fans expecting a thrilling battle. The West Indies come into this series riding high on confidence but with unfinished business in T20Is. They were outclassed at home by England in their last series and will be desperate to set the record straight. Nicholas Pooran has been nothing short of sensational, smashing sixes for fun and surpassing Chris Gayle's record for most T20 sixes in a calendar year. Brandon King is in fine touch, but his opening partner - be it Andre Fletcher ​​​​​or Johnson Charles - needs to fire. Skipper Rovman Powell has had his ups and downs, but the likes of Keacy Carty and the red-hot Justin Greaves add depth to their batting lineup and both could be in line to make their debuts. All-rounders Romario Shepherd and Roston Chase bring balance to the side, while Alzarri Joseph’s fiery pace and Obed McCoy’s clever variations form a lethal pace attack. The spin duo of Akeal Hosein and Gudakesh Motie could prove decisive on home soil. Bangladesh, however, will be hungry to bounce back after a heartbreaking ODI series. Soumya Sarkar has been in scintillating form, fresh off his heroics in the Global Super League T20. Skipper Mehidy Hasan, along with Litton Das and Jaker Ali, will anchor the batting, but this is also a chance for rising stars like Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan to shine. Taskin Ahmed was a standout in the Test series, and Bangladesh will hope he carries that momentum into the T20Is. Hasan Mahmud and Tanzim Hasan Sakib bolster the pace attack, while the towering leg-spinner Rishad Hossain could be the X-factor. Will the Bangla Tigers roar back to life, or will the Windies continue their winning spree? It’s all set for an explosive start - who are you backing?
